value.title: Change a live Copilot seat's reasoning effort
value.summary: Relaunch a running Copilot seat on a new `--effort` in the same pane, resuming the same conversation, with its pij identity and cache-proxy environment kept. Replaces docs/how/change-seat-effort.md.

value.who: The operator, or the prime or the seat's parent with the operator's yes. Never the seat itself: the relaunch ends its own process.
value.when: When the operator wants a live Copilot seat on a different effort without losing its context. Run it with `--key <seat>`.

value.name: effort
value.description: the effort, one of none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh or max (`copilot --help`, --reasoning-effort); anything else is refused. Which ones work depends on the model

value.title: Get the operator's yes
value.done_when: The operator agreed to relaunch this seat now.

value.title: Relaunch the seat in its pane on the new effort
value.done_when: The seat's process runs with exactly `--effort <effort>`, resumed on the same session, in the same pane.

pre.fix: Wait until `pij list` shows the seat idle with an empty composer; only Copilot seats take this procedure.

value.proven_in_practice: By hand on pij-capable-marten, 2026-11-23, by the prime (medium to xhigh). The script is tested against stub tools (relaunch.test.ts) but has not yet run on a live seat.

value.title: Check it re-registered with its context
value.done_when: `pij list` shows the seat on its new process with its extension build, and its footer shows the new effort with the context figure unchanged.

sections.name: done_when
sections.value: The seat runs on the new effort, resumed with its context, and pij lists it registered on the new process.

value.text: pij keeps the old recorded effort, so a later `pij-rs revive` puts the seat back on it; `revive --effort` does not exist yet.

pij records the relaunched seat as plain, not proxied: the new process doesn't descend from the launch the daemon stamped (F213). Its traffic still goes through the cache proxy, because the COPILOT_PROVIDER_* environment came with it (check with `ps -Eww -p <pid>`).
The relaunched process runs without `pij-rs __spawn-child`, so if it exits there is no exit-status file or launch log for a post-mortem.
The seat's flags come from `ps`, which joins arguments with spaces, so a flag value that holds a space comes back as two words.

A PIJ_* or COPILOT_* variable whose name holds KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASS, CREDENTIAL or AUTH is not carried (req-13). The script names each one it leaves out; a seat that needs one must get it again another way.
Dropping the COPILOT_PROVIDER_* environment: the seat silently leaves the cache proxy and its next wake after five minutes idle rebuilds its whole context.
Carrying PIJ_SPAWN_ID: it ties the new process to a spawn that has finished.
Leaving out --resume=<session>: the seat starts a new conversation and loses its context.
Using `/settings effortLevel` (changes the default for every new session) or `/restart` (keeps the old flag).

Putting the seat's environment on the respawn command line: every value is then readable through `ps` by any local user and logged by the endpoint scanner. The script passes values through a 0600 file the pane reads and deletes.
